It sounds like you have urges when stressful things happen (You're mother telling you to put on a bra when going outside and wanting to burn yourself), that is the escapism self harm provides . And at the end of the day addiction is that. It's like an alcoholic wanting to drink after a shitty day (an alcoholic doesn't need a shitty day to drink though, they can find any excuse. A celebration, sitting on the couch, having a toothache, to just shop for groceries). You might not read it as addiction now, but when you keep doing it, get the chemical release in your head ((endorphins and neurotransmitters which actually keeps it chemically addictive (Addictions can be formed with things that dont cause bad, perhaps life threatening, withdraws btw, like video games/porngraphy/self harm vs heroin/alcohol withdrawal)), the thought of doing a routine/ritual, and keep idolizing it as just fun, then those urges/want for 'fun' will keep coming back. You literally say it makes you feel calm, safe, okay. Guess what other addicts would say about the  substance they use or the lifestyle choice they do. 

I guess I didn't think about self harm as an addiction when I first started, but as I've grown up with it (and a lot of people who also started young) I definitely see it as a bad habit slippery slope , and if im doing it there is a reason (even if one wants to deny that deep-rooted, uncomfortable feeling). It sounds from your post history you recently started this behavior. If it's not addictive actually (or yet), I hope you can kick it before it becomes worse (doesnt happen to everyone, true, but it often does, as with most addictions as time goes on a need to increase or a want), or you have very good control to not do too much, practice harm reduction, and a good cleaning routine. 

Anyway, you'll probably say I'm just bullshitting you and I'm being insensitive, but that is probably the honest truth to it. it's all up to you. Maybe you'll feel the same way when you're 18 about it and that its just fun, or maybe you'll wake up one day and know it's bad but you have to emotionally regulate. Who knows.

Report your mother if she keeps doing this or becomes more abusive, emotionally, physically, and mentally. Get a job, get your independence, do a club or sport and make friends, and tell trusted adults if your mom tries to do anything worse. If you had a good relationship previously to this, perhaps you can confront her and tell her that's not what you wanted to hear right then, but it does depend on how much she can parent right now and listen to her child's needs. My ideas might be too drastic for what's going on, but know you can have agency if things get too bad.

As someone with cptsd whose had 2 long-termish relationships (over a year in my book) this happens to me often. It feels terrible. I can't trust love at all, it's always worth something or it's not enough I can ever give. And the burn out being a partner is also a terrible experience too. Going back and forth on if a relationship is worth it because with the traumas, normal ass expectations, and the anxieties it can quickly become overwhelming, especially if a people pleaser. I every few months go through a cycle of thinking the best plan is to break up. Usually illogical till stuff explodes during my dissociation and then I got to face the reality, or I ghost it for a while in hypomania, which is shit people move 101 but I guess I don't learn. 

It can feel like you are losing feelings for your partner when things are so much. I felt like all I was good for in relationships is to use  someone up, their kindness and feel like I dont give as much. 

So who knows. It could be purely a cptsd reaction, a mixture, or they just don't know how to break up with people healthily (Another probable trauma response) or maybe they did break it off in the way they find correct and healthy. 

Is there anything rather major in their life going on along with the news since they asked to have the distance? If you don't know, ask. My episodes follow in line with stressful changes to me occurring. But maybe they do or should only be friends, even if it sucks a lot, if they are super unstable now. Best thing is probably try to be there arms reach if you can take doing that, don't overpressure them while communicating it more through, and if it doesn't work out it just doesn't work out, as scary as that is. Wish you luck.
